chat_history.content:
Given are 3 files and a link: https://service.mattel.com/instruction_sheets/BJV44-Eng.pdf revolving around the game blokus that my team and i are programming for a uni class. 

We are working on sharpening our requirements that are split into two milestones (milestone 1 for the base game and milestone is the change request for two player). We let another LLM analyze the content for ambiguity which is why the ambiguity log is included. Update the two specifications based on the team answers in the ambiguity log. Notice that at times, we reference the game rules (the link). Add the logic from the rules to the appropriate locations whenever necessary.

Updated both specification files (SPEC_M1 and SPEC_M2) from v1.0 to v2.0, resolving all ambiguity log items and embedding official Blokus rules from Mattel rulebook BJV44.

Summary of changes:

SPEC_M1:
- FR-1.4 (AMB-01): Replaced vague 'color continuity rules' with four explicit sub-rules from BJV44: diagonal corner-touch required, same-color edge-sharing prohibited, different-color contact unrestricted, placed pieces immovable.
- FR-3.4 (AMB-02): Replaced '(e.g., ...)' placeholder with a concrete three-priority deterministic heuristic: maximize squares placed → maximize future corner-touch points → lexicographic tie-break.
- FR-4.1 (AMB-01/rules): Embedded piece set composition, clockwise turn order, pass rule, and game-end condition from BJV44.
- FR-4.2 (AMB-03/rules): Explicit corner assignments per color: Blue→(0,0), Yellow→(0,19), Red→(19,19), Green→(19,0).
- FR-4.3 (AMB-04): Defined post-termination sequence: stop input → calculate scores → announce winner → prompt replay or exit.
- FR-4.4 (AMB-05): Locked to basic scoring scheme (lowest remaining squares wins); bonus scoring excluded; tie-handling defined.
- NFR-1.1–1.3 (AMB-06): Added Reference Environment block defining targets relative to standard modern laptop.
- IR-1.1 (AMB-08): Replaced vague 'structured branching strategy' with concrete feature-branch policy.

SPEC_M2:
- Scope clarification (AMB-03): M2 implements the official Classic two-player variant (20x20 board, two colors per player), not the separate Blokus Duo product.
- FR-1.1b/FR-4.1b: Explicit sub-rules from BJV44: Player 1=Blue+Red, Player 2=Yellow+Green; fixed turn order Blue→Yellow→Red→Green; per-color rules apply independently; combined scoring.
- CR-R1–R5: Board stays 20x20, two players each controlling two colors, same four corner assignments, 42 pieces per player, fixed turn sequence added.
- Section 4.2/AMB-07: Replaced 'no code duplication' with clear reuse-first policy.
can you able to convert this chat history into a json file such that i can recreate this chat at a later time?

metadata.topic: Blokus Game Engine — Requirements Specification Update
metadata.context_summary: The user is a university student working on a Blokus game engine project. Their team had an LLM generate an ambiguity log (AMBIGUITY_LOG.md) against two requirement specs (SPEC_M1 for the base 4-player Classic game, SPEC_M2 as a change request for a two-player variant). The assistant read all three files plus the official Mattel Blokus rulebook (BJV44-Eng.pdf) and updated both specs to v2.0, resolving all 8 ambiguity items and embedding the official game rules into the appropriate requirements.
